title: Define billing semantics for prefetch reservoirs and multiplexed mini-batches
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: As we increase speculative prefix prefetching and allow request multiplexing into small ‘mini-batches’ to improve utilization, customers and sales have reported confusing and sometimes incorrect-looking invoices and quota consumption. Current metering attributes tokens to the final microbatch that executed, which fails to capture transient reservoir work (prefetches that never contributed to an output) and misattributes shared compute in multiplexed mini-batches.

Goal: Define and implement clear, auditable billing semantics that: (1) charge for actual inference work tied to a customer’s request when it contributes to response tokens, (2) attribute a small, transparent reservation cost for prefetch reservoir work that materially reduces future token cost, and (3) prorate shared mini-batch compute deterministically when multiple tenants or streams are multiplexed.

Scope: This ticket covers design, telemetry, and a narrow-first implementation for hosted and dedicated modes (not private on-prem packaging). The scope includes metering rules, accounting code markers, test harness changes, API changelog text, console invoice language, and rollout plan. Not included: pricing model negotiation with finance (handled by Pricing PM).
acceptance_criteria: Updated metering spec documented and approved by Finance/PM/Legal
Server-side metering emits new 'reservoir_reserved_tokens' and 'mini_batch_shared_units' fields for every batch event
Billing calculation prototype that demonstrates identical charges for a 10k-run workload under old vs new rules for a baseline (no prefetch, no multiplexing)
Regression tests that catch double-charging for requests that hit the KV cache after prefetch reservoir activity
Console invoice text updated with an explanatory note and example line items for reservoir reservations
No customer-visible change to token SLOs; rate limiter counters adjusted to use new per-request provenance
design_decisions: Reserve-and-commit model: prefetch reservoirs will be charged using a two-line accounting flow — a low-cost reservation line (reservoir_reserved_tokens) at the time of prefetch and a commit/credit line (reservoir_commit_tokens) when those tokens yield output. If the prefetch never contributes, the reservation is billed at a pre-specified discount rate.

Deterministic prorate for multiplexed mini-batches: when N logical owners share compute in a mini-batch, charge proportionally to estimated token-provenance weights derived from per-request token counts and observed KV hit fractions. Use integer-safe rounding rule to ensure sums equal the batch cost.
Backwards-compatible telemetry: emit both legacy 'token_count' and new provenance-attributed fields for six weeks of overlap to support backfill reconciliation and customer comparisons.

Atomic charge boundaries: all accounting records will be idempotent and keyed by a 'charge_boundary' UUID produced when the request enters the routing/aggregation layer. This allows replays and retries without double-counting.

Conservative default: until customers opt into discounted reservoir pricing, reservations will be billed at a conservative default rate to avoid revenue loss. Finance will expose an opt-in discount flag controlled by plan/contract.
telemetry_queries: SQL: SELECT count(*) FROM metering_events WHERE event_type='mini_batch' AND tags->>'shared'='true'
Dataflow: sample trace events where reservoir_reserved_tokens > 0 and final_token_count == 0 to estimate wasted reservation fraction
Kusto: metering | where event_time between (start, end) | summarize sum(reservation_cost) by customer_id
test_plan: Unit tests for cost attribution functions (edge rounding, zero-contribution prefetch)
Integration test harness that simulates 10k synthetic requests across cache-hit/cold/prefetch scenarios and validates invoice lines against golden accounting
Chaos test: inject duplicate batch events and ensure idempotent accounting via charge_boundary UUID
Load test: measure overhead of additional provenance fields on metering pipeline and ensure 95th percentile ingestion latency < 500ms
Customer scenario validation: run subset of closed customer traces through the new accounting to show expected delta < 2% for non-prefetch workloads
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Canary, week 0): Emit new metering fields in telemetry for 5% of customers, no billing impact (fields only). Monitor anomalies and reconciliation deltas.
Phase 2 (Pilot, week 2): Enable reservation billing (discounted rate) for internal & pilot customers under opt-in flag. Run side-by-side billing calculations and report diffs to Finance dashboard.
Phase 3 (Gradual rollout, week 4-6): Turn on full accounting for 50% of customers in staged cohorts; enable reconciliation job to adjust any over/under charges detected during pilot.
Phase 4 (GA, week 8): Switch off legacy-only telemetry after 6 weeks of overlap; publish console explanations, docs, and migration notes. Backfill reconciliation run for pilot customers if necessary.
